lessons.title: चांगला (chāṅglā) — good
lessons.gloss: good — the ordinary word of approval, and the one बरं could never quite be

segments.text: बरं has been in this book since chapter four and it can only say that a STATE is fine — मी बरा आहे. It cannot call a thing good.

segments.instruction: say sundar khoolī, then name the class सुंदर belongs to
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say *sundar khoolī*, then name the class **सुंदर** belongs to]

segments.text: चांगला — chāṅglā — good.
चांगला चहा, चांगली खोली, चांगलं घर — chāṅglā chahā, chāṅglī khoolī, chāṅglaṁ ghar.
It ends in -आ, so it agrees, and you already know all three forms without being told them. That is the second time the rule has paid for itself.

Keep it apart from बरं. बरं answers how are you and closes a turn — fine, all right, okay. चांगला (chāṅglā) is a judgement about a thing: this tea is good, that room is good, he is a good friend. English blurs the two under good and Marathi does not.

segments.instruction: baraṁ and chāṅglā back to back, and name what each is for
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *baraṁ* and *chāṅglā* back to back, and name what each is for]

segments.prompt: Say 'good tea' and 'a good room', then claim the tea is good.
acceptedResponses: chāṅglā chahā; chāṅglī khoolī; chahā chāṅglā āhe
चांगला चहा चांगली खोली चहा चांगला आहे

feedback.incorrect: chahā is masculine, khoolī feminine — the ending follows.

segments.text: Which of बरं and चांगला (chāṅglā) judges a THING? (चांगला (chāṅglā).) Which class does चांगला (chāṅglā) belong to? (The agreeing one — it ends in -आ.)
Sources: Wiktionary: चांगला (chāṅglā).

lessons.title: खराब (kharāb) — bad, spoiled
lessons.gloss: bad, spoiled — an Arabic word that reached Marathi through Persian, and a third one that never agrees

segments.text: Half a judgement is not a judgement. You can say a thing is good and not that it is not.
खराब — kharāb — bad, spoiled, ruined.
खराब पाणी — kharāb pāṇī — bad water.

Its last letter tells you it will not agree, before you ever hear it used: खराब (kharāb) खोली, खराब (kharāb) घर, no ending anywhere. Three adjectives into the class now, and the test has not failed you once.

This one carries its history on its face. It is the Arabic kharāb, "ruined, in ruins," and it reached Marathi through Persian — the same road that brought मदत and हरकत, both of which this book has already taught. Centuries of Persian administration in the Deccan left several hundred such words in ordinary Marathi.
The original sense survives in the modern one. खराब (kharāb) is closer to spoiled than to evil: bad water, a bad road, a phone that has stopped working.

segments.instruction: pāṇī kharāb āhe, then pāṇī chāṅglaṁ nāhī
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *pāṇī kharāb āhe*, then *pāṇī chāṅglaṁ nāhī*]

segments.instruction: which language it came from, and by which road — Arabic, through Persian
segments.source: [YOU SAY: which language it came from, and by which road — **Arabic, through Persian**]

segments.prompt: Say the water is bad, then that the water is not good.
acceptedResponses: pāṇī kharāb āhe; pāṇī chāṅglaṁ nāhī
पाणी खराब आहे पाणी चांगलं नाही

feedback.incorrect: kharāb never changes; chāṅglā agrees with neuter pāṇī.

segments.text: Does खराब (kharāb) agree? (No — it does not end in -आ.) Which two taught words came by the same road? (मदत and हरकत.)
Sources: Wiktionary: खराब (kharāb).

lessons.title: हुशार (hushār) — clever
lessons.gloss: clever, sharp — the first word this book has for what a PERSON is like rather than a thing

segments.text: Everything you can describe so far is a thing. The A1 speaking paper asks you to describe a person for a minute.
हुशार — hushār — clever, sharp, quick-witted.
माझा मित्र हुशार आहे. — mājhā mitra hushār āhe. — my friend is clever.

Another one that does not agree, and by now you saw that coming from the last letter. It is the sixth adjective this book has taught and the fourth that does not agree; the invariable class is already twice the size of the other one, which is worth knowing so the endings stop feeling like the default.

हुशार (hushār) is the Persian hushyār, "alert, wide awake," built on hush, "consciousness, wits." Marathi kept the alertness inside the cleverness: a हुशार (hushār) person is quick rather than merely learned, and it is what a teacher says about a child who catches on fast.
It is a compliment you can pay out loud without awkwardness, which is not true of every word in this area, and it is exactly the kind of thing the speaking paper's one-minute description wants.

segments.instruction: say puṇyāhūn and that your clever friend comes from Pune
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say *puṇyāhūn* and that your clever friend comes from Pune]

segments.prompt: Say that your friend is clever and good.
acceptedResponses: mājhā mitra hushār āhe; mājhā mitra chāṅglā āhe
माझा मित्र हुशार आहे माझा मित्र चांगला आहे

feedback.correct: One agrees, one does not, in the same frame.
feedback.incorrect: hushār never changes; chāṅglā matches masculine mitra.

segments.text: What does the Persian hush inside it mean? (Wits, consciousness — so clever is awake.) Does it agree? (No.)
Sources: Wiktionary: हुशार (hushār).

lessons.title: Say what you think of something
lessons.gloss: judge a thing, judge a person, and negate either one

segments.text: Three more adjectives. Two of them cannot change and one can. Say which is which before you use any of them.

segments.instruction: chahā chāṅglā āhe — and hear the masculine ending
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *chahā chāṅglā āhe* — and hear the masculine ending]

segments.instruction: pāṇī kharāb āhe — and hear that nothing was added
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *pāṇī kharāb āhe* — and hear that nothing was added]

segments.instruction: sundar, lahān, kharāb, hushār — the four that never move
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *sundar*, *lahān*, *kharāb*, *hushār* — the four that never move]

segments.instruction: say udyāpāsūn and promise something from tomorrow
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say *udyāpāsūn* and promise something from tomorrow]

segments.prompt: Judge a thing good, judge a thing bad, judge a person clever, then deny one of them.
acceptedResponses: chahā chāṅglā āhe; pāṇī kharāb āhe; mājhā mitra hushār āhe; pāṇī chāṅglaṁ nāhī
चहा चांगला आहे पाणी खराब आहे माझा मित्र हुशार आहे पाणी चांगलं नाही

feedback.correct: Two judgements, a person, and a denial.
feedback.incorrect: Only chāṅglā takes an ending; negate by ending on nāhī.

segments.text: Of the six adjectives you now own, how many agree? (Two — मोठा and चांगला (chāṅglā).) What do the other four have in common? (None of them ends in -आ.)
